ev.q: In 2020, 14 million (27.6%) older adults reported falling during the previous year.
The percentage of women who reported falling (28.9%) was higher than that among men (26.1%).
The fall-related death rate was higher among men (91.4 per 100,000) than among women (68.3).
In 2021, 38,742 (78.0 per 100,000) older adults died as the result of unintentional falls.
The percentage of women reporting falls was significantly higher than that for men in five states.
Age-adjusted percentages and death rates were calculated using the direct method and 2000 U.S. Census Bureau standard population.
BRFSS is a landline/mobile telephone survey which collects information about health-related behavioral risk factors
NVSS extracts data from death certificates filed in the 50 states and DC.

methods_quotes.q: Age-adjusted percentages and death rates were calculated using the direct method and 2000 U.S. Census Bureau standard population.
Statistical comparisons between percentages were made using two sample t-tests as appropriate for complex survey designs such as BRFSS.
Death rates were compared using a z-test when counts were >100.
Monte Carlo simulation was employed as a third method of assessing rate differences.
Statistical comparisons between national and state estimates were made by removing the state’s estimate from the national estimate to account for nonindependence.
